<p class="page-lead">I combine comparative genomics, phylogenetics, protein-structure analysis, and machine learning to study virus evolution and build reusable discovery systems.</p>

<section class="work-themes">
<header class="work-section-heading"><span>Research interests</span><h2>Three connected directions</h2></header>
<div class="work-theme-grid">
<article><h3>Viral elements in eukaryotic genomes</h3><p>Reconstructing past virus–host interactions from integrated viral sequences and their distribution across eukaryotic lineages.</p></article>
<article><h3>Virus evolution and comparative genomics</h3><p>Using genome-scale and phylogenetic evidence to understand viral diversity, host range, and evolutionary history.</p></article>
<article><h3>AI-assisted protein discovery</h3><p>Combining protein language models with sequence, structure, and cluster-aware validation for interpretable discovery.</p></article>
</div>

<section class="work-projects">
<header class="work-section-heading"><span>Selected projects</span><h2>From question to evidence</h2></header>

<article class="work-project" id="djr-finder">
<header><span>Protein discovery · 2026–present</span><h2>DJR-Finder</h2><p>AI-assisted recognition and validation of double jelly-roll proteins.</p></header>
<dl class="work-project-facts">
<div><dt>Problem</dt><dd>Sequence divergence makes viral major capsid proteins and related double jelly-roll proteins difficult to identify reliably at scale.</dd></div>
<div><dt>My role</dt><dd>Designed the end-to-end modelling and validation workflow.</dd></div>
<div><dt>Approach</dt><dd>Frozen ESM-2 embeddings, calibrated linear classifiers, cluster-aware data splitting, HMMER, and Foldseek.</dd></div>
<div><dt>Outcome</dt><dd>Unified protein recognition, capsid classification, and conditional viral taxonomy prediction in one reproducible system.</dd></div>
</dl>
<div class="evidence-links"><span>Code and manuscript links will be added when public.</span></div>
</article>

<article class="work-project" id="eve-landscape">
<header><span>Comparative genomics · 2025–present</span><h2>Endogenous dsDNA viral landscape</h2><p>A large-scale view of viral elements embedded in eukaryotic genomes.</p></header>
<dl class="work-project-facts">
<div><dt>Problem</dt><dd>Endogenous elements derived from dsDNA viruses remained poorly characterised across eukaryotes.</dd></div>
<div><dt>My role</dt><dd>Led dataset design, pipeline development, comparative analysis, validation, and manuscript preparation.</dd></div>
<div><dt>Approach</dt><dd>Screened 37,254 public eukaryotic genomes and standardised 781,111 viral regions from 7,103 assemblies.</dd></div>
<div><dt>Outcome</dt><dd>Revealed broad but lineage-specific accumulation and previously unrecognised virus–host associations.</dd></div>
</dl>
<div class="evidence-links"><a href="https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.04.19.649669">Preprint</a><a href="./publications.html">Publication details</a></div>
</article>

<article class="work-project" id="mirusvirus">
<header><span>Virus–host range · 2023–2024</span><h2>Mirusvirus host-range research</h2><p>Genomic evidence for a wider diversity and ecological range of mirusviruses.</p></header>
<dl class="work-project-facts">
<div><dt>Problem</dt><dd>Mirusviruses were known mainly from marine metagenomes, while their potential eukaryotic hosts remained uncertain.</dd></div>
<div><dt>My role</dt><dd>Led the first-author computational study and integrated sequence, structure, and phylogenetic evidence.</dd></div>
<div><dt>Approach</dt><dd>Screened 1,901 eukaryotic genome assemblies for marker genes and examined high-confidence capsid signals and circular genomes.</dd></div>
<div><dt>Outcome</dt><dd>Expanded the known host range across eight eukaryotic supergroups and diverse environments.</dd></div>
</dl>
<div class="evidence-links"><a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2024.04.085">Paper</a><a href="./publications.html">Publication details</a></div>
</article>
</section>
</div>
